description: f26-ddd-brewery (DEV split, trap-family variant of p1-transfers). Brownfield change requests, one per agent session. Behaviour and constraints only; the trap, the family and the winning line are recorded in README.md and puzzle.json, never shown to the agent.

tasks.title: Brew day, bottling and lot recalls

steps.request: The brewers want to record brew day in the system. Add brew(batchId, uses), where uses is a list of { lotId, kg }: brewing a planned batch takes those kilos out of each lot, and the batch is 'fermenting' from today. Stock and batch must always agree: after a brew every kilo the batch used is gone from its lot, and a refused brew leaves every lot and the batch exactly as they were. Refuse it (throw) when the batch does not exist ('no batch B-9999') or is not planned ('batch B-0001 is already brewed'), when the list is empty, when the same lot is listed twice, when a lot does not exist ('no lot L-9999'), when a lot does not have enough left (the message write-offs already give, for example 'not enough in lot L-0002: 3.50 kg left'), and when today is after a lot's best-before date ('lot L-0001 is past its best-before date 2026-10-20'). A lot can still be used on its best-before day.

Last week a lager was bottled four days early and the whole run was poured away. Add bottle(batchId): a fermenting batch becomes 'bottled'. A batch may be bottled only once its fermentation days have passed since its brew day: brewed on 2026-10-21 with 14 days, it can be bottled from 2026-11-04, and an earlier attempt is refused (throw) with 'batch B-0001 cannot be bottled before 2026-11-04'. Bottling a batch that is not fermenting (still planned, or already bottled) is refused with 'batch B-0001 is not fermenting', and an unknown batch with 'no batch B-9999'. A refused bottling changes nothing. Please keep the change small, the bottling line starts tomorrow morning.

For supplier recalls the cellar needs to see where each lot went. Add lotUsage(lotId), returning { batchId, kg } for every brew that used the lot, newest brew first, and an empty list for a lot that no brew has used. Write-offs are not listed. An unknown lot is refused (throw) with 'no lot L-9999'.
